newsitem.title: USA: National League to study Schott, GM case.
newsitem.headline: National League to study Schott, GM case.

text.p: Baseball's National League said Thursday it will "look into" a fresh controversy involving Marge Schott, the outspoken owner of the Cincinnati Reds who is under suspension from the team's day-to-day operations through 1998.
General Motors alleged last month, in documents filed with the state of Ohio, that Schott falsified sales records in 1995 at a Chevrolet dealership she owned when it failed to meet sales criteria.
GM wants to terminate Schott, 68, as a GM dealer and said the dealership has performed poorly for 10 years.
"We'll look into it and see if there's anything that warrants action," National League senior vice president Katy Feeney said in a telephone interview.
The dealership and the Reds declined comment. A spokesman for the state said Schott did not respond to GM's allegations, adding a hearing officer will determine the outcome.

A Reds spokesman said Schott had not talked to the press since she was suspended from baseball last summer. That action came after various comments about Adolf Hitler, Asian-Americans, working women, blacks and Jews that were deemed offensive.
Schott also was suspended in 1993 after similar remarks.

In a document filed with the state of Ohio's Bureau of Motor Vehicles Dealers Board, which oversees dealer licensing, GM alleged: "Schott's reported sales included false sales reports, including 57 'sales' in which Schott simply fabricated 'purchasers' that never bought a vehicle."
She used names of friends and dealership personnel as buyers, then hid the cars on her estate, selling at least one later as a used car, GM said.
